exclusions.text: All other uses of the bio-engineered skin and soft tissue substitutes listed above do not meet the definition of medical necessity.

notes: Built from the single clean copy in the PDF (no redline/tracked-changes copy is present). effective_date is the printed Revised date 10/01/26 and reviewed_date the printed Reviewed date 04/23/26, as in the hand-built example; the printed Original Effective Date is 01/01/01.
Scope: the document says it does not address meshes or patches of non-biologic origin used for standard repair procedures such as hernia repairs.

Pathways: one per indication the position statement grants (breast reconstruction ADM; diabetic lower extremity ulcers; venous insufficiency ulcers; dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa; second- and third-degree burns; nonhealing diabetic ulcers with human amniotic membrane; collagen-based dressing). Each product bullet is its own leaf under an 'any' so a code maps to a leaf; no document-level general block exists.

Code tags: every code printed with '(Investigational)' in the coding section is tagged investigational (364 codes). The 45 codes printed without that mark are tagged covered: product codes of position-statement products (Q4101, Q4102, Q4105, Q4107, Q4110, Q4114, Q4116, Q4121, Q4122, Q4128, Q4132, Q4133, Q4137, Q4151, Q4154, Q4158, Q4159, Q4160, Q4186, Q4187, Q4283, Q4304, A2019), the application codes 15271-15278 and G0681-G0684, the not-otherwise-specified product codes A4100, Q4431, Q4432, Q4433, and the collagen dressing codes A6010, A6011, A6021-A6024. 'Covered' means covered for the indication of the pathway that names the code; all other uses do not meet medical necessity (exclusion 1).

Judgment call, unmarked codes whose descriptor also names an investigational product: Q4133 (Grafix prime ... stravix and stravixpl; Stravix is on the investigational list), Q4151 (Amnioband or guardian; Guardian/AmniBand is on the investigational list), Q4128 (Flex hd, or allopatch hd), A2019 (Kerecis omega3 marigen shield; Alphaplex with MariGen Omega3 is on the investigational list). Tagged covered because the document does not mark the code, and mapped to the pathway of the covered product the code names (Grafix, AmnioBand Membrane, FlexHD/AlloPatch, Kerecis Omega3). A reviewer could read A2019 as a different Kerecis product and tag it investigational.

Judgment call, NOS codes: A4100, Q4431, Q4432 and Q4433 describe an unspecified product and are printed without an investigational mark; tagged covered and mapped to every product pathway (not collagen) because the position-statement products that have no product code of their own (AlloMend, Cortiva, DermaMatrix, Dermagraft, mVASC, OrCel, Epicel) could only be billed through them. Coverage then turns on the product leaf in the pathway.

Judgment call, application codes: 15271-15278 and G0681-G0684 are tagged covered and mapped to the five wound-treatment pathways (diabetic ulcer, venous ulcer, epidermolysis bullosa, burns, amniotic membrane DFU), not to breast reconstruction or collagen dressings. The Reimbursement section says they must be submitted with product codes and are denied with an investigational product; that conditional denial ('For products considered experimental or investigational, the application codes (15271-15278, G0681-G0684) will also be denied.') is recorded as an exclusion with no codes rather than as a tag; its text is cut at 'application codes' because the PDF breaks the line inside 'G0681-G0684' and the verbatim check cannot match across that hyphenation.

Judgment call, reimbursement limits in the tree: 'Apligraf is limited to five (5) applications per ulcer', 'Dermagraft is limited to eight (8) applications per treatment site over a twelve (12) week period', OrCel single application and no more than eight pieces per donor site, and 'Dressings are limited to 26 units per treatment site per 6-month period' are quantities a chart can show, so they are criteria attached to the product (or collagen) branch they name. 'Safety and effectiveness of re-treatment of a single wound using Apligraf, Dermagraft or OrCel ... is considered experimental or Investigational' is both an exclusion and a not-leaf on those three product branches. 'Collagen-based dressings or wound fillers ... can stay in place up to 7 days' is left out (usage, not a requirement).

Judgment call, compound indication phrases kept as one criterion: 'chronic, non-infected, full-thickness diabetic lower extremity ulcers' and 'chronic, noninfected, partial- or full-thickness lower extremity skin ulcers due to venous insufficiency' hold several adjectives a chart must support; they are kept as one leaf each (the question asks for all parts) because splitting into one-word criteria would not be verbatim-meaningful. The venous ulcer sentence's 'which have not adequately responded following a one-month period of conventional ulcer therapy' is a separate leaf with a one-month duration threshold.

Judgment call, 'when there is insufficient tissue expander or implant coverage by the pectoralis major muscle and additional coverage is required' is kept as one criterion: the 'and' clause is the consequence of the first, not a second finding.

Judgment call, HDE clauses: 'when provided in accordance with the Humanitarian Device Exemption (HDE) specifications of the FDA' (OrCel) and 'when provided in accordance with the HDE specifications of the FDA' (Epicel) are answerable: false because the HDE specifications live in FDA labeling, not in a chart; the clinical parts of each HDE indication (mitten-hand deformity, failed standard therapy; deep dermal/full-thickness burns >= 30% TBSA) are their own answerable leaves.

Judgment call, 'Nonhealing' definition: 'less than a 20% decrease in wound area with standard wound care for at least 2 weeks' is split into a number leaf (< 20%) and a duration leaf (standard wound care >= 2 weeks, recorded as 0.5 months because thresholds for treatment trials are in months).

Left out of the tree: the Description / Summary and Analysis of Evidence section (evidence narrative, not requirements); the footnotes '* Banked Human Tissue', '** FDA premarket approval', '*** FDA 510(k) clearance', '**** FDA-approved under an HDE' (regulatory status, not chart requirements); the Program Exceptions (FEP, SAO, Medicare Advantage follow other documents, recorded in excluded_plans); the step therapy protocol exemption paragraph (Florida law 627.42393; a process, not a criterion); the Related Guidelines, References and update history.

Exclusion 3 (injection of micronized/particulated human amniotic membrane; injection of human amniotic fluid) lists only the codes whose descriptor is an injectable amniotic product (Q4139 AmnioMatrix/BioDMatrix injectable, Q4145 Epifix injectable, Q4206 Fluid flow or fluid GF, an amniotic fluid product on the investigational list); other per-mg/per-cc amniotic codes are investigational by their table mark and are carried by exclusion 4.

Exclusion 4 ('All other bio-engineered skin substitutes ... are considered experimental or investigational, including, but not limited to:') carries every code the coding section marks investigational; the bulleted product list itself is not a coding list and is not re-typed.
Dermagraft is covered by the position statement for diabetic ulcers but has no product code in this document's coding section (the update history records Q4106 deleted 01/01/26).
The ICD-10 list is the document's 'ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes That Support Medical Necessity' table, ranges as printed.
